comments.author: Theo
comments.body:
Inflation makes things expensive, true, but it also encourages production. Knowing that if today I build a carro at 1m, I could sell it tomorrow for 3m.

Deflation, on the other hand, would severely discourage production. Why would I spend 300k to make a carro 16, knowing that tomorrow I could only sell it for 200k, or risking nobody being able to afford it...

When the production ends, people just quit.

comments.author: Lancelot
comments.body:
That doesn't hold up. Nobody will sell anything for 200k when it cost them 300k to make. Selling price lowers when and only when production cost lowers.

Look, it's not greed that drives prices up. I can want to sell a particular item for 1 billion all I want, but if the average player only has 50 million or so, and super rich only have 750 million, then the item will never sell, no matter how desireable the item is. The ONLY thing that drives prices up to the degree we have been seeing is the sheer amount of ducats circulating in the game. This holds true in real life as well. It is why it is such a terrible idea for any government to go printing money willy-nilly and turning it loose into the market.

comments.author: Jean
comments.body: the natural "burn down" is deflation by definition btw, and it is in no way keeping up. The ONLY thing that will bring prices down is for the circulated coin to decrease. Not only will taking the ducats out of the system work, it is the only thing that will work.

comments.author: Erda
comments.body:
ESBT or dungeon is not the root cause of the inflation. The lack of disciplines of some people who plays 24/7 and abuse the ESBT and dungeon system is the root cause.

What about introducing a cool down on dungeon entries to once an hour and could accumulate up to 5 times? This way, it makes abusing dungeon counter-productive (with 1 hour waiting time), but it rarely affects everyone else.

comments.body:
"Extinguish the fire which represents me." These words are etched into the newly installed sky-blue torches found in Fort San Domingo's upper floor! After examining the sky-blue torch, red ones light up throughout the room, and you have to match the description of a discovery with the picture last shown, hopefully without triggering enmity 100.

And hidden in the upper floor's hidden passages (which you can apparently run consecutively, but watch your stamina gauge as thin air can deplete it quickly!) is a new two-star Treasure discovery, "Kaoliang Wine". There might be more, but it's all I've found so far. On to the mysteries of the middle floor!
